## Quantization formats (97)

- **AQLM (additive / multi-codebook quantization)** (`quantization/aqlm`) — 2, 3 and 4-bit weights (targeting sub-4-bit); activations remain fp16, so this is w2a16 / w3a16 · From the paper's abstract: AQLM is 'the first scheme that is Pareto optimal in terms of accuracy-vs-model-size when compressing to less than 3 bits per parameter' and 'significantly improves upon all known schemes in the extreme compression (2bit) regime'. No specific perplexity number in the abstract; none recorded.
- **AWQ (activation-aware weight quantization)** (`quantization/awq`) — w4a16 · From the AWQ paper itself, OPT-6.7B under INT3-g128: WikiText perplexity 43.2 for plain RTN vs 13.0 when the salient 1% of weights are identified by activation distribution and kept in FP16; AWQ's per-channel scaling is the hardware-efficient alternative to that mixed-precision layout (quant-awq-paper). No fp16-vs-AWQ delta number was quoted in the abstract, so no second figure.
- **Accuracy cost of quantization: measured deltas on named benchmarks** (`quantization/qhw-accuracy-cost-summary`) — varies by method · SUMMARY OF MEASURED ACCURACY DELTAS: (1) Marlin INT4 (Llama2-7B, WikiText-2): 5.12 (FP16) vs 5.27 (INT4) = +0.15 ppl. MMLU: 41.80 vs 40.07 = -1.73. (2) GPTQ 3-bit (Llama-7B, WikiText-2): 5.68 (FP16) vs 8.07 (3-bit) = +2.39 ppl. With group-128: 6.61 = +0.93 ppl. (3) SpQR 3-4 bit (LLaMA, Falcon): <1% perplexity loss. (4) SignRound 2-bit: 6.91-33.22% improvement over RTN across 11 tasks. (5) LLM-FP4 (LLaMA-13B, commonsense zero-shot): 63.1 vs 68.9 (FP16) = -5.8 points. (6) SpinQuant W4A4KV4 (LLaMA-2-7B, zero-shot): 64.0 vs 66.9 (FP16) = -2.9 points. (7) QuaRot W4A4KV4 (LLaMA2-70B, WikiText-2): 0.29-0.47 ppl increase. (8) KIVI 2-bit KV: 'almost the same quality' (qualitative). (9) KVQuant 3-bit KV: <0.1 ppl degradation. (10) AWQ INT3 (OPT-6.7B, WikiText-2): 43.2 (RTN) vs 13.0 (AWQ) = -30.2 ppl improvement over RTN. The pattern: 4-bit weight-only quantization typically costs 0.1-0.3 ppl on WikiText-2. 3-bit costs 0.5-1.0 ppl. 2-bit costs 2.0+ ppl. KV cache quantization at 4-bit is nearly lossless; at 2-3-bit it costs 0.1-0.5 ppl. The accuracy cost is model-dependent and benchmark-dependent.
- **Atom (mixed-precision block-outlier low-bit quantization for serving)** (`quantization/atom`) — w4a4 (4-bit weights AND 4-bit activations) with mixed-precision outlier channels retained at higher precision · From the abstract: end-to-end throughput up to 7.73x versus FP16 and 2.53x versus INT8 quantization at the same latency target, with negligible accuracy loss, in the serving context. These are throughput figures from the authors' own system on their own kernels - vendor-style numbers, not independent. No perplexity figure in the abstract.
- **AutoRound (Intel) - SignRound weight-rounding PTQ toolkit, W4A16 and neighbours** (`quantization/autoround-w4a16`) — W2A16 / W3A16 / W4A16 / W5A16 / W6A16 / W7A16 / W8A16, all defined as bits=N, group_size=128, sym=True, act_bits=16. Plus NVFP4 (group_size 16), MXFP4/MXINT4/MXFP4_RCEIL/MXFP8 (group_size 32, flagged 'research feature, no real kernel'), FP8_STATIC, FP8_BLOCK, FPW8A16 (group_size 0 = per-tensor) · Vendor claim, one controlled number with a named model: the INT2-mixed DeepSeek-R1 (~200GB) retains 97.9% accuracy (OPEA/DeepSeek-R1-int2-mixed-sym-inc, qlab2-autoround-step-by-step). Methodology (benchmark, eval set, baseline) is not stated in the source, so treat it as vendor-claim-grade. Everything else in the README is either a speed claim about quantization cost or a pointer to a leaderboard.
- **BitNet b1.58 (ternary LLM)** (`quantization/bitnet-b158`) — 1.58 avg · From the paper, as a training result rather than a post-training delta: BitNet b1.58 'matches the full-precision (i.e., FP16 or BF16) Transformer LLM with the same model size and training tokens in terms of both perplexity and end-task performance', while being 'significantly more cost-effective in terms of latency, memory, throughput, and energy consumption' (quant-bitnet-paper). This is a matched-size-and-token-budget training claim, NOT an fp16-inference-baseline delta, and it is the paper's own headline rather than an independent replication.
- **CacheGen (KV cache tensor encoding + bandwidth-adaptive streaming)** (`quantization/cachegen`) — adaptive per-part compression level; the paper reports a 3.5-4.3x reduction in KV cache SIZE with negligible response-quality impact · From the abstract: reduces KV cache size by 3.5-4.3x and total delay in fetching and processing contexts by 3.2-3.7x, with negligible impact on LLM response quality, versus systems that reuse the KV cache.
- **DuoAttention (head-wise retrieval/streaming KV sparsity) - NOT KV quantization** (`quantization/duoattention-kv-sparsity`) — none by default - retrieval heads keep a full KV cache, streaming heads use a lightweight CONSTANT-LENGTH KV cache. The paper's headline long-context result is achieved combined WITH quantization. · From the abstract: reduces long-context inference memory by up to 2.55x for MHA and 1.67x for GQA, speeds decoding by up to 2.18x (MHA) and 1.50x (GQA), and accelerates pre-filling by up to 1.73x (MHA) and 1.63x (GQA), with minimal accuracy loss. Combined with quantization, it enables LLaMA-3-8B decoding at 3.3 million context length on a single A100 GPU.
- **EXL2 (GPTQ with mixed per-tensor bitrate)** (`quantization/exl2`) — 2-8 adjustable (target average bits-per-weight, e.g. 2.5 / 3.0 / 4.0 / 5.0 bpw builds)
- **ExLlamaV2 EXL2 kernel throughput benchmarks (3090 Ti / 4090)** (`quantization/qhw-exllama-throughput`) — 2-8 bpw (adjustable average bits-per-weight)
- **FLUTE (lookup-table engine for LUT-quantized LLMs)** (`quantization/flute`) — non-uniform 3-bit weight-only (also applied as an extension of NormalFloat quantization); activations fp16 · No direct quality number in the abstract. As an application of the engine the paper extends NormalFloat quantization and quantizes LLaMA3 'obtaining competitive quantization performance against strong baselines while obtaining an end-to-end throughput increase of 1.5 to 2x'. Quality is described only comparatively; none recorded.
- **FP8 E4M3 (per-tensor / per-block scaled)** (`quantization/fp8-e4m3`) — w8a8 (fp8 weights, fp8 activations, fp32 accumulate) · No controlled fp16 delta was located in the primary sources read for this record. Vendor checkpoint claims (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8 et al. shipped by NVIDIA) exist but are not a perplexity comparison, so none recorded.
- **FP8 E5M2** (`quantization/fp8-e5m2`) — w8a8 (or, in practice, KV-cache format)
- **FP8 KV cache quantization (E4M3 keys and values)** (`quantization/qhw-fp8-kv-cache`) — 8-bit KV cache (E4M3 format for both keys and values) · No controlled benchmark with named accuracy delta found in the sources accessed. The vLLM quantization docs list 'Quantized KV Cache' as a supported feature but do not publish accuracy figures. The SGLang docs mention FP8 KV cache support but similarly lack quantitative accuracy data. This is a significant gap: FP8 KV cache is widely deployed but the accuracy impact is not well-documented in public sources.
- **FP8 block scaling (blockwise, E4M3 with per-block scale)** (`quantization/fp8-blockwise`) — w8a8, block-scaled
- **GGUF IQ1_M (1.75 bpw trellis-flavoured 1-bit with 3-bit sub-block scales and a grid-shift bit)** (`quantization/gguf-iq1-m`) — 2.1460 measured avg (llama.cpp quantize README, Llama-3.1-8B); official tool string '1.75 bpw quantization'. block_iq1_m = { uint8_t qs[QK_K/8]; uint8_t qh[QK_K/16]; uint8_t scales[QK_K/32]; } = 32 + 16 + 8 = 56 bytes / 256 = 1.75 bpw · Official tool string '1.75 bpw quantization' (qlab2-quantize-options-table); no controlled fp16 delta published. Null + note.
- **GGUF IQ1_S (1.5625 bpw, non-linear 1-bit-ish with a 16-bit grid high plane)** (`quantization/gguf-iq1-s`) — 2.0042 measured avg (llama.cpp quantize README, Llama-3.1-8B); official tool string '1.56 bpw quantization'. block_iq1_s = { ggml_half d; uint8_t qs[QK_K/8]; uint16_t qh[QK_K/32]; } = 2 + 32 + 16 = 50 bytes / 256 = 1.5625 bpw · Official tool string '1.56 bpw quantization' (qlab2-quantize-options-table); no controlled fp16 delta published. Null + note.
- **GGUF IQ2_M (mixture built on IQ2_S with Q4_K/Q5_K promoted tensors)** (`quantization/gguf-iq2-m`) — 2.9294 measured avg (llama.cpp quantize README, Llama-3.1-8B); official tool string '2.7 bpw quantization'. NOT a distinct block type - llama_tensor_get_quant_type maps LLAMA_FTYPE_MOSTLY_IQ2_M to GGML_TYPE_IQ2_S · Official tool string '2.7 bpw quantization' (qlab2-quantize-options-table); no controlled fp16 delta published. Null + note.
- **GGUF IQ2_S (2.5625 bpw, non-linear 2-bit with a 4-bit scale per 64 and sign/high-bit planes)** (`quantization/gguf-iq2-s`) — 2.7403 measured avg (llama.cpp quantize README, Llama-3.1-8B); official tool string '2.5 bpw quantization'. block_iq2_s = { ggml_half d; uint8_t qs[QK_K/4]; uint8_t qh[QK_K/32]; uint8_t scales[QK_K/32]; } = 2 + 64 + 8 + 8 = 82 bytes / 256 = 2.5625 bpw · Official tool string '2.5 bpw quantization' for IQ2_S and '2.7 bpw quantization' for IQ2_M (qlab2-quantize-options-table); no controlled fp16 delta published. Null + note.
- **GGUF IQ2_XXS (2.0625 bpw, almost-true 2-bit with a 16-bit scale per 256)** (`quantization/gguf-iq2-xxs`) — 2.3824 measured avg (llama.cpp quantize README, Llama-3.1-8B); official tool string '2.06 bpw quantization'. block_iq2_xxs = { ggml_half d; uint16_t qs[QK_K/8]; } = 2 + 64 = 66 bytes / 256 = 2.0625 bpw · Official tool string '2.06 bpw quantization' (qlab2-quantize-options-table); no controlled fp16 delta published. Null + note.
- **GGUF IQ3_S (3.4375 bpw, non-linear 3-bit with separate sign plane)** (`quantization/gguf-iq3-s`) — 3.6606 measured avg (llama.cpp quantize README, Llama-3.1-8B); official tool string '3.44 bpw non-linear quantization'. block_iq3_s = { ggml_half d; uint8_t qs[QK_K/4]; uint8_t qh[QK_K/32]; uint8_t signs[QK_K/8]; uint8_t scales[IQ3S_N_SCALE]; } with IQ3S_N_SCALE = QK_K/64 = 4 · Official tool string '3.44 bpw non-linear quantization' for IQ3_S and '3.66 bpw quantization mix' for IQ3_M (qlab2-quantize-options-table). No controlled fp16 delta published. Null + note.
- **GGUF IQ3_XXS (3.0625 bpw, almost-true 3-bit with a 16-bit scale per 256)** (`quantization/gguf-iq3-xxs`) — 3.2548 measured avg (llama.cpp quantize README, Llama-3.1-8B); official tool string '3.06 bpw quantization'. block_iq3_xxs = { ggml_half d; uint8_t qs[3*QK_K/8]; } = 2 + 96 = 98 bytes / 256 = 3.0625 bpw · Official tool string '3.06 bpw quantization' (qlab2-quantize-options-table); no controlled fp16 delta published. Null + note.
- **GGUF IQ4_NL (non-linear 4-bit, 32-value blocks, QK4_NL)** (`quantization/gguf-iq4-nl`) — 4.6818 measured avg (llama.cpp quantize README, Llama-3.1-8B); official tool string '4.50 bpw non-linear quantization'. Block layout: QK4_NL = 32, block_iq4_nl = { ggml_half d; uint8_t qs[QK4_NL/2]; } = 18 bytes / 32 = 4.5 bpw · Official tool string only: IQ4_XS '4.25 bpw non-linear quantization' and IQ4_NL '4.50 bpw non-linear quantization' (qlab2-quantize-options-table). No controlled fp16 delta is published for IQ4_NL in any primary source found; the llama.cpp quantize README reports IQ4_NL text generation at 76.63 t/s and prompt processing at 806.03 t/s on CPU for Llama-3.1-8B but that is a speed number, not a quality delta. Null + this note rather than a guessed delta.
- **GGUF IQ4_XS (non-linear 4-bit, 256-value super-block with 6-bit sub-block scales)** (`quantization/gguf-iq4-xs`) — 4.4597 measured avg (llama.cpp quantize README, Llama-3.1-8B); official tool string '4.25 bpw non-linear quantization'. block_iq4_xs = { ggml_half d; uint16_t scales_h; uint8_t scales_l[QK_K/64]; uint8_t qs[QK_K/2]; } = 2 + 2 + 4 + 128 = 136 bytes / 256 = 4.25 bpw · Official tool string '4.25 bpw non-linear quantization' (qlab2-quantize-options-table); no controlled fp16 perplexity delta published in any primary source found. Null + note.
- **GGUF Q2_K / Q2_K_S (2-bit K-quant)** (`quantization/gguf-q2-k`) — 2.625 effective bpw for block_q2_K (source comment); 2.9697 measured avg for Q2_K_S and 3.1593 for plain Q2_K on Llama-3.1-8B (llama.cpp quantize README) · Only the unified Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct study was found for the 2-bit K-quant tier. The closest measured point is Q3_K_S (3.9960 bpw, same family): WikiText-2 ppl 8.96 vs 7.32 FP16, GSM8K 68.31 vs 77.63, IFEval 71.87 vs 78.93, unweighted 5-benchmark mean 65.49 vs 69.47 (quant-gguf-kquant-study). No published perplexity for plain Q2_K/Q2_K_S was located, so none recorded.
- **GGUF Q3_K_M (3-bit K-quant, medium)** (`quantization/gguf-q3-k-m`) — 3.9960 measured avg (llama.cpp quantize README, Llama-3.1-8B). The pure block_q3_K is 3.4375 bpw (source comment); the measured 3.9960 is Q3_K_M, a MIXTURE of q3_K and wider types. · Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, one checkpoint, official llama.cpp toolchain, vs its own F16 baseline (quant-gguf-kquant-study): WikiText-2 ppl 7.96 vs 7.32 (+0.64); GSM8K 75.03 vs 77.63 (-2.60); HellaSwag 73.16 vs 72.51; IFEval 73.41 vs 78.93; MMLU 77.19 vs 63.50; TruthfulQA 54.56 vs 54.79; unweighted mean 68.07 vs 69.47. Size 3825 MiB vs 15317 MiB F16 (-75.03%).
- **GGUF Q4_0 (legacy block-4 symmetric)** (`quantization/gguf-q4-0`) — 4.5 (classic block format; Q4_0 measured 4.4597 bpw in the IQ sweep, Q4_0 as a legacy 4-bit type is quoted as ~4) · Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (quant-gguf-kquant-study): WikiText-2 ppl 7.74 vs 7.32 F16; GSM8K 71.03 vs 77.63 (-6.60); IFEval 71.88 vs 78.93; mean 67.98 vs 69.47; size 4438 MiB (-71.03%).
- **GGUF Q4_1 / Q5_1 (legacy asymmetric 32-value blocks with per-block scale AND min)** (`quantization/gguf-legacy-q4-1`) — 4.5 bpw for q4_1 (QK4_1 = 32: 2 x fp16 + 16 = 36 bytes / 32 values), 5.5625 bpw for q5_1 (2 x fp16 + 4 + 16 = 40 bytes / 32) · Official quantizer strings: Q4_0 '4.34G, +0.4685 ppl @ Llama-3-8B', Q4_1 '4.78G, +0.4511 ppl', Q5_0 '5.21G, +0.1316 ppl', Q5_1 '5.65G, +0.1062 ppl', Q8_0 '7.96G, +0.0026 ppl' (qlab2-quantize-options-table). All are the tool's own Llama-3-8B deltas; note Q4_1's +0.4511 vs Q4_0's +0.4685 is a 0.017 ppl gain for 0.44 GB.
- **GGUF Q4_2 / Q4_3 (REMOVED types, type ids 4 and 5 reserved as DEPRECATED)** (`quantization/gguf-deprecated-q4-2-q4-3`) — n/a - removed. The enum slots survive as .type_name = "DEPRECATED" with blck_size = 0, type_size = 0, is_quantized = false · n/a - no quality figure is published for a removed type; recorded as deprecated rather than given a fabricated delta. The live legacy figures are in the sibling records (gguf-q4-0, gguf-legacy-q4-1).
- **GGUF Q4_K_M (4-bit K-quant, medium)** (`quantization/gguf-q4-k-m`) — 4.8944 measured avg (llama.cpp quantize README, Llama-3.1-8B). The pure block_q4_K is 4.5 bpw (source comment); 4.8944 is the Q4_K_M mixture. · Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (quant-gguf-kquant-study): WikiText-2 ppl 7.56 vs 7.32 F16 (+0.24, the smallest perplexity cost of any 4-bit option measured); GSM8K 69.41 vs 77.63; IFEval 72.35 vs 78.93; unweighted mean 69.15 vs 69.47 (-0.46% AvgLoss); size 4685 MiB (-69.41%).
- **GGUF Q4_K_S (4-bit K-quant, small)** (`quantization/gguf-q4-k-s`) — 4.6672 measured avg (llama.cpp quantize README, Llama-3.1-8B); pure block_q4_K is 4.5 bpw · Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (quant-gguf-kquant-study): WikiText-2 ppl 7.62 vs 7.32 F16 (+0.30); GSM8K 70.83 vs 77.63; HellaSwag 77.33 vs 72.51; IFEval 72.79 vs 78.93; MMLU 80.26 vs 63.50; TruthfulQA 53.40 vs 54.79; unweighted mean 69.17 vs 69.47 (-0.43% AvgLoss); size 4468 MiB (-70.83%).
- **GGUF Q5_K_M (5-bit K-quant, medium)** (`quantization/gguf-q5-k-m`) — 5.7036 measured avg (llama.cpp quantize README, Llama-3.1-8B); pure block_q5_K is 5.5 bpw · Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (quant-gguf-kquant-study): WikiText-2 ppl 7.40 vs 7.32 F16 (+0.08); GSM8K 64.35 vs 77.63 (-13.28, the study's clearest multi-step-reasoning regression among the 5-bit tier); IFEval 72.33 vs 78.93; unweighted mean 69.36 vs 69.47; size 5460 MiB (-64.35%).
- **GGUF Q6_K (6-bit K-quant)** (`quantization/gguf-q6-k`) — 6.5633 measured avg (llama.cpp quantize README, Llama-3.1-8B); block_q6_K is 6.5625 bpw (source comment) - Q6_K is essentially a pure type · Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (quant-gguf-kquant-study): WikiText-2 ppl 7.35 vs 7.32 F16 (+0.03, within noise); unweighted mean 69.23 vs 69.47; size 6283 MiB (-58.98%). GSM8K reported 58.98 vs 77.63 for F16, which is a 18-point drop inconsistent with a +0.03 perplexity change and with the paper's own claim that Q6_K is near-baseline - treat the Q6_K GSM8K cell as unverified.
- **GGUF Q8_0 (legacy block-8 symmetric)** (`quantization/gguf-q8-0`) — 8.5008 avg (llama.cpp measured, Llama-3.1-8B) · Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (quant-gguf-kquant-study): WikiText-2 ppl 7.33 vs 7.32 F16 (+0.01); unweighted mean 69.41 vs 69.47 (-0.09% AvgLoss); size 8138 MiB (-46.87%). This is the reference-ish GGUF baseline: 8.5008 bpw includes block scales, so it is genuinely close to lossless.
- **GGUF TQ1_0 / TQ2_0 (ternarized quants, QK_K super-block, trit-packed)** (`quantization/gguf-tq1-0`) — TQ1_0 1.6875 bpw, TQ2_0 2.0625 bpw (both from the struct comments in ggml-common.h). Quantize tool strings: TQ1_0 '1.69 bpw ternarization', TQ2_0 '2.06 bpw ternarization' · Official quantizer strings only (qlab2-quantize-options-table): TQ1_0 '1.69 bpw ternarization', TQ2_0 '2.06 bpw ternarization'. No controlled fp16 perplexity delta published in any primary source found. Null + note.
- **GGUF imatrix (importance matrix) - the calibration file that determines WHICH weights get more bits** (`quantization/gguf-imatrix`) — not a format - a per-tensor activation-energy file. It changes the effective bits of an existing quant choice, not the nominal bits of a type · n/a - the imatrix is a calibration artifact, not a quantization format, so it has no quality_delta of its own. Its effect is to REMOVE part of the quantization delta of the format it is applied to. IMPORTANT: the official per-type ppl strings in the llama.cpp quantizer (Q4_K_M +0.1754, Q5_K_M +0.0569, Q6_K +0.0217, Q8_0 +0.0026 on Llama-3-8B) are measured WITH the standard imatrix workflow, so those figures already include imatrix benefit and must not be quoted as no-imatrix numbers.
- **GPTQ (one-shot approximate second-order PTQ)** (`quantization/gptq`) — w4a16 headline; also reported at w3a16 (and 2-bit / ternary) in the paper's extreme regime. Weight-only - activations are NOT quantized. · From the GPTQ paper: OPT-175B and BLOOM-176B quantized to 3-4 bits in ~4 GPU hours with 'minimal increase in perplexity'; the bespoke execution kernels give ~3.25x on A100 and 4.5x on A6000 (quant-gptq-paper). The paper's Figure 1 is a ppl-vs-RTN comparison against the FP16 baseline and is a figure, not tabulated numbers, so no single delta value is recorded here. ADDITIONAL SOURCED FIGURES (qlab-gptq-paper, arXiv 2210.17323 read directly): the paper quantizes 175B-parameter models in approximately four GPU hours, reducing bitwidth to 3 or 4 bits per weight with negligible accuracy degradation, and 'allows us for the first time to execute a 175 billion-parameter model inside a single GPU'. It also explicitly claims reasonable accuracy in the extreme regime 'in which weights are quantized to 2-bit or even ternary quantization levels' - this is the primary source for the GPTQ 3-bit and ternary results, and the reason GPTQ belongs in the sub-4-bit family even though its headline is 4-bit. From the reference implementation (qlab-gptq-github), LLaMa-7B Wiki2 perplexity: FP16 5.68, 4bit-GPTQ 6.09, 3bit-GPTQ 8.07, 3bit group-128 GPTQ 6.61. The last pair is the load-bearing comparison: 3-bit works or does not depending on GROUP SIZE, not on the algorithm. Both are authors' own numbers, not independent replication.
- **H2O (heavy-hitter KV eviction) - NOT KV quantization** (`quantization/h2o-kv-eviction`) — none - no bits are reduced. Evicts tokens instead. Retains a configurable budget of heavy-hitter plus recent tokens (20% heavy hitters in the paper's throughput results). · From the abstract: with 20% heavy hitters, H2O improves throughput over DeepSpeed Zero-Inference by up to 29x, HuggingFace Accelerate by up to 29x, and FlexGen by up to 3x on OPT-6.7B and OPT-30B; at the same batch size it reduces latency by up to 1.9x. Validated across OPT, LLaMA and GPT-NeoX. The 29x figures are against systems whose baselines are far weaker, so they mostly measure the baseline gap, not H2O.
- **HQQ (half-quadratic quantization)** (`quantization/hqq`) — 1-8: nbits supports 8, 4, 3, 2 and 1 (qlab2-hqq-readme). Commonly 2/3/4. · Only a cross-model claim, not a controlled fp16 delta: HQQ-quantized Llama-2-70B at 2-bit is reported as outperforming full-precision Llama-2-13B at comparable memory (quant-hqq-blog). The comparable controlled claim is speed: HQQ quantizes Llama-2-70B in under 5 minutes, reported as >50x faster than GPTQ (quant-hqq-blog).
- **INT8 KV cache quantization (8-bit keys and values)** (`quantization/qhw-int8-kv-cache`) — 8-bit KV cache (INT8 format for both keys and values)
- **INT8 W8A8 (weight-only scheme, per-tensor / per-channel)** (`quantization/int8-w8a8`) — w8a8
- **INT8 W8A8 rowwise / per-channel** (`quantization/int8-channelwise`) — w8a8
- **InfiniGen (speculative KV prefetch for offloaded serving) - NOT KV quantization** (`quantization/infinigen-kv`) — none - no bits reduced. Reduces how much of the KV cache must be FETCHED from host memory. · From the abstract: improves overall performance of a modern offloading-based system by up to 3.00x compared to prior KV cache management methods, while offering 'substantially better model accuracy'. No accuracy number given; none recorded.
- **Intel Neural Compressor (multi-technique PTQ/QAT toolkit; low-bit LLM path is AutoRound)** (`quantization/neural-compressor-stack`) — the toolkit spans INT8 / FP8 / MXFP8 / INT4 / MXFP4 / NVFP4 plus sparsity; its own advanced low-bit LLM/VLM quantization is DELEGATED to AutoRound · n/a - the README cites 'Faster Inference of LLMs using FP8 on the Intel Gaudi' (arXiv:2503.09975) but does not restate a delta inline. Null + note rather than paraphrasing a paper I did not read for this record.
- **KIVI (2-bit key / 4-bit value KV cache, per-channel keys, per-token values)** (`quantization/kivi-kv2`) — 2-bit keys / 4-bit values - ASYMMETRIC, and the asymmetry is the paper's central finding · From the abstract: KIVI lets Llama, Falcon and Mistral maintain 'almost the same quality' while using 2.6x less peak memory (INCLUDING model weight), which enables up to 4x larger batch size and brings 2.35x-3.47x throughput on a real LLM inference workload. No perplexity figure in the abstract; 'almost the same quality' is qualitative and unquantified here.
- **KVQuant (per-channel + pre-RoPE key quantization, non-uniform KV)** (`quantization/kvquant`) — 3-bit keys and values are the headline (<0.1 perplexity degradation); the method is a toolkit that also supports 2-bit and 4-bit · From the abstract: '<0.1 perplexity degradation with 3-bit quantization on both Wikitext-2 and C4', outperforming existing approaches, across LLaMA, Llama-2, Llama-3 and Mistral. Enables serving LLaMA-7B at up to 1 million context on a single A100-80GB and up to 10 million on an 8-GPU system.
- **LLM-FP4 (4-bit floating-point W4A4 PTQ, pre-Blackwell)** (`quantization/llm-fp4`) — w4a4 (both weights and activations quantized to 4-bit FLOATING POINT, post-training) · From the abstract: quantizes both weights and activations of LLaMA-13B to 4-bit, achieving an average score of 63.1 on commonsense zero-shot reasoning tasks, 'only 5.8 lower than the full-precision model' and 'significantly outperforming the previous state-of-the-art by 12.7 points'. Authors' own numbers; no independent replication located.
- **LLM-QAT (data-free quantization-aware training, NVIDIA)** (`quantization/llm-qat`) — w4a4 to w8a8 plus 4-bit KV cache (per-tensor/per-channel groups configured per experiment) · Paper states 'large improvements over training-free methods, especially in the low-bit settings' for LLaMA 7B/13B/30B down to 4-bit. The abstract gives no numeric perplexity delta and the experiments section was not read this session, so no number is recorded here. Third-party comparisons elsewhere cite LLM-QAT trailing W4A4 by ~22 points of zero-shot accuracy, but that figure is from SpinQuant's table, not from this paper.
- **LLM-QAT KV cache quantization (4-bit KV inside a QAT regime)** (`quantization/llm-qat-kv-cache`) — 4-bit KV cache, alongside quantized weights and activations
- **LLM.int8() / bitsandbytes int8 (vector-wise with 16-bit outliers)** (`quantization/bitsandbytes-int8`) — w8a16 (mixed-precision decomposition: >99.9% of values multiplied in 8-bit, outlier dims in fp16) · From the primary paper (qlab-llmint8-paper): a 175B-parameter 16/32-bit checkpoint can be loaded, converted to Int8 and used immediately with no performance degradation, because the mixed-precision decomposition keeps 'more than 99.9% of values multiplied in 8-bit' while the outlier dimensions go through fp16. The authors frame the entire result as 'it is possible to perform inference in LLMs with up to 175B parameters without any performance degradation'. No numeric benchmark delta is tabulated in the abstract, so no perplexity or accuracy number is recorded here.
- **LQER (low-rank quantization error reconstruction)** (`quantization/lqer`) — w4a8 (4-bit weights, 8-bit activations) - claimed near-lossless · From the abstract: 'near-lossless W4A8 quantization on various LLMs and downstream tasks' without knowledge distillation, grid search, or gradient iterative optimization; near-lossless on six downstream tasks while using 1.36x fewer hardware resources than the leading state-of-the-art method. No per-task numbers in the abstract; none recorded.
- **MLC LLM compiler quantization (q4f16 group-quant, plus q3f16, AWQ, FP8 per-tensor and FP8 block-scale)** (`quantization/mlc-quant-q4f16`) — q4f16_* = int4 weights / fp16 activations with group_size 32; q3f16_* = int3 with group_size 40; q4f16_autoawq = AWQ with group_size 128; q4f16_ft = faster-transformer int4-in-int8; e4m3_e5m2_f16 = FP8 W8A8 per-tensor; fp8_e4m3fn_bf16_block_scale = FP8 blockwise · n/a - MLC publishes no controlled fp16 quality delta in the registry or the intro docs. Null + note.
- **MXFP4 (OCP microscaling FP4, E8M0 scale)** (`quantization/mxfp4`) — w4a4 · No inference fp16 delta recorded from a controlled benchmark. The closest primary evidence is a PTQ study of SmoothQuant+AWQ+GPTQ applied to MX formats, which reports 4-bit weights with 8-bit activations in MXINT with 'negligible accuracy loss compared to the uncompressed baseline' (quant-mx-ptq-paper) - that is the authors' own qualitative wording, not a number, and it concerns MXINT (8-bit) rather than MXFP4 specifically. NVIDIA's own comparison rates MXFP4 as carrying 'risk of noticeable accuracy drop compared to FP8' where NVFP4 does not (quant-nvfp4-blog), which is a vendor ranking, not a measurement.
- **MXFP4 MoE quantization: per-expert scales and block scaling for mixture-of-experts** (`quantization/qhw-moe-mxfp4`) — w4a4 (MXFP4 weights and activations for MoE layers)
- **MXFP4 vs NVFP4: block size, scale format, and hardware support comparison** (`quantization/qhw-mxfp4-vs-nvfp4`) — w4a4 (both weights and activations quantized to 4-bit floating point) · NVIDIA's own comparison (from the NVFP4 blog) rates MXFP4 as carrying 'risk of noticeable accuracy drop compared to FP8' where NVFP4 does not. The scale-encoding MSE is 0.72 for E8M0 (MXFP4) vs 0.08 for E4M3 (NVFP4). This is a vendor ranking, not a measurement. No independent controlled benchmark comparing MXFP4 and NVFP4 on the same model with the same calibration data was found.
- **MXFP6 (OCP microscaling FP6, E3M2/E2M3 + E8M0)** (`quantization/mxfp6`) — 6-bit elements in 32-value blocks with a shared power-of-two scale; used as one channel of a mixed-precision MX pipeline, typically alongside MXFP4 and MXFP8 · None recorded. The source paper states 'competitive or superior performance across diverse downstream tasks, including zero-shot and few-shot learning, language modeling, code generation, and mathematical reasoning' without a named numeric delta in the abstract.
- **MXFP8 (OCP microscaling FP8, E4M3 + E8M0)** (`quantization/mxfp8`) — w8a8, block-scaled
- **Machete Hopper-optimized mixed-precision GEMM kernel (CUTLASS-based)** (`quantization/qhw-machete-kernel`) — w4a16 (4-bit weights, FP16 activations) - same precision as Marlin but optimized for Hopper SM90
- **Marlin INT4 weight-only kernel (FP16xINT4 mixed-precision GEMM)** (`quantization/qhw-marlin-kernel`) — w4a16 (4-bit weights, FP16 activations) · From the Marlin README benchmark table (Llama2 models, INT4 group=128): 7B WikiText-2 5.12 (FP16) vs 5.27 (INT4), RedPajama 6.14 vs 6.30, MMLU 41.80 vs 40.07. 13B: WikiText-2 4.57 vs 4.67, RedPajama 5.67 vs 5.79, MMLU 52.10 vs 51.13. 70B: WikiText-2 3.12 vs 3.21, RedPajama 4.74 vs 4.81, MMLU 65.43 vs 64.81. These are GPTQ-quantized models evaluated with Marlin kernels, so the delta includes both quantization error and any kernel-specific effects.
- **Microsoft Olive (Onnx LIVE) - hardware-targeted ONNX optimization / quantization composer** (`quantization/olive-quant-stack`) — not a single format: Olive runs search over conversion + quantization passes and emits whichever ONNX quant configuration wins for the declared target. Quantization algorithms were expanded in Olive 0.8.0 (2025-03) and again in 0.9.2 (2025-08) · n/a - no quality delta published. Null + note.
- **MoE mixed-precision expert bit allocation (expert-level bit-width, not one fixed precision)** (`quantization/moe-mixed-precision`) — per-expert or per-expert-group bit widths. The published endpoints span 2.25-bit (MxMoE), ~2-bit (MoQE, AlphaQ, EAQuant W2A4) and 4-bit W8A8-style expert weights; AutoScheme generates mixed-bit recipes in minutes · The only figures in this cluster with a named model, benchmark and delta are from MxMoE (qlab2-arxiv-mxmoe): 2.4 lower Wikitext-2 perplexity than GPTQ at 2.25-bit, up to 3.4x speedup over full precision, and up to 29.4% speedup over uniform quantization at equivalent accuracy with 5-bit weight-activation quantization. Model architectures are not named in the abstract, so treat as paper-claim-grade. MoQE (qlab2-arxiv-moqe) reports an INT2-mixed DeepSeek-R1-sized MoE at 79.6% model-size reduction vs fp16 and 1.24x A100 speed-up with an optimized runtime, but gives no benchmark name.
- **MoE routing-instability under quantization (VSRAQ / EAQuant routing-consistency alignment)** (`quantization/moe-routing-quant-interaction`) — not a distinct format - a PTQ OBJECTIVE that constrains which bit-allocations are acceptable, used on top of otherwise-standard schemes at W4A4 / W3A4 / W3A3 / W2A4 · EAQuant reports average accuracy improvements of 1.15-13.81% over existing methods across three MoE architectures at W4A4/W3A4/W3A3/W2A4, with the largest gains on reasoning tasks (qlab2-arxiv-eaquant). Architectures and benchmark names are not given in the abstract - paper-claim-grade, model unnamed.
- **NVFP4 (Blackwell block-scaled E2M1 + E4M3)** (`quantization/nvfp4`) — w4a4 (fp4 weights and fp4 activations with hardware-native block-scaled tensor-core path) · NVIDIA, DeepSeek-R1-0528, FP8 vs NVFP4, seven benchmarks (vendor-reported): MMLU-Pro 85% vs 84%, GPQA Diamond 81% vs 80%, HLE 15% vs 14%, LiveCodeBench 77% vs 76%, SciCode 40% vs 40%, Math-500 98% vs 98%, AIME 2024 89% vs 91%. The blog states this as '1% or less accuracy degradation versus FP8' (quant-nvfp4-blog). This is a vendor comparison against an FP8 baseline, not against fp16, and is vendor-claim-grade.
- **NVIDIA Model Optimizer (ModelOpt) quantization recipes** (`quantization/modelopt`) — w4a16 / w4a8 / w8a8 / w4a4-fp4 depending on the recipe (FP4, FP8 per-tensor, FP8 block scaling, FP8 rowwise, NVFP4, W4A16/W4A8 AWQ, W4A16/W4A8 GPTQ)
- **ONNX Runtime GenAI model-builder quantization paths (int4, fp8, ModelOpt/compressed-tensors ingest)** (`quantization/ortgenai-int4-fp8`) — int4 (MatMulNBits weight-only, block size selectable), fp16/bf16/fp32 I/O, plus direct ingest of an already-quantized AutoGPTQ/AutoAWQ checkpoint and of a ModelOpt or compressed-tensors NVFP4/FP8 checkpoint · n/a - the builder README documents no numeric quality delta. Null + note.
- **ONNX Runtime INT4/UInt4 via MatMulNBits and GatherBlockQuantized (weight-only, blockwise)** (`quantization/ort-matmulnbits-int4`) — 4-bit weights (Int4 if is_symmetric=True, else UInt4). Block size must be a power of two >= 16; the documented example is block_size=128 · n/a - no numeric delta published by Microsoft. Null + note.
- **ONNX Runtime quantization toolset (quantize_static / quantize_dynamic, QDQ vs QOperator)** (`quantization/ort-quant-int8`) — 8-bit weights and activations. Four sign combinations: U8U8, U8S8, S8U8, S8S8. reduce_range=True drops weights to 7 bits on non-VNNI AVX2/AVX512 · n/a - none published. The ORT docs deliberately describe the failure modes instead: 'it is not rare to get worse performance on old devices', and quantization is called 'not a loss-less transformation'. Null + this note.
- **OmniQuant (learnable weight clipping + equivalent transformation)** (`quantization/omniquant`) — reported at w2a16, w3a16, w4a16, w4a4, w6a6 and w8a8 (paper enumerates these configurations) · Paper states LLaMA-2 7B-70B is processed within 1-16 hours on a single A100-40G using 128 samples, and validates across w2a16/w3a16/w4a16/w4a4/w6a6 without naming a headline accuracy number in the abstract. No numeric quality delta recorded.
- **Pensieve (multi-tier conversation-state KV cache) - NOT KV quantization** (`quantization/pensieve`) — none - no bits reduced. Retains and reuses conversation state across requests in a multi-tier cache. · From the abstract: 1.14x-3.0x the throughput of vLLM and TensorRT-LLM with significantly reduced latency, in the multi-turn conversation setting.
- **PyramidKV (layer-dependent KV budget) - NOT KV quantization** (`quantization/pyramidkv`) — none - allocates different KV cache SIZES per layer (more in lower layers, less in higher ones) rather than reducing bits. · From the abstract: matches full-KV-cache performance on LongBench while retaining only 12% of the KV cache; at an extreme 0.7% retention it surpasses other KV compression techniques with up to 20.5 absolute accuracy improvement on TREC; retaining just 128 KV entries gives LLaMA-3-70B 100.0 accuracy on Needle-in-a-Haystack.
- **QServe / QoQ (W4A8KV4 quantization and system co-design)** (`quantization/qserve-w4a8kv4`) — w4a8kv4 (4-bit weights, 8-bit activations, 4-bit KV cache) - explicitly named QoQ, quattuor-octo-quattuor, i.e. 4-8-4 · From the abstract: QServe improves maximum achievable serving throughput of LLaMA-3-8B by 1.2x on A100 and 1.4x on L40S, and Qwen1.5-72B by 2.4x on A100 and 3.5x on L40S, versus TensorRT-LLM. The paper also quantifies the problem it solves: existing INT4 methods suffer 20-90% runtime overhead from dequantizing weights or partial sums on GPUs. Throughput figures from the authors' own system; no perplexity number in the abstract.
- **QServe SmoothAttention (4-bit KV cache with an accuracy-preserving correction)** (`quantization/qserve-kv4`) — 4-bit KV cache (keys and values), the 'KV4' of W4A8KV4 · Throughput figures only in the abstract (LLaMA-3-8B 1.2x on A100 / 1.4x on L40S vs TensorRT-LLM; Qwen1.5-72B 2.4x on A100 / 3.5x on L40S). No KV-specific quality number in the abstract.
- **QuARX (GPU-efficient 4-bit-weight / 8-bit-activation quantization) - UNVERIFIED PLACEHOLDER** (`quantization/quarx`) — w4a8 (believed; not confirmed against a primary source)
- **QuIP# (Hadamard incoherence processing + E8 lattice codebooks)** (`quantization/quip-sharp`) — 2, 3 and 4-bit weight-only (<=4 bits per weight); activations fp16 · The abstract claims 'state-of-the-art results in extreme compression regimes (<=4 bits per weight)', 'enables new behaviors in PTQ scaling', and 'supports fast inference', with no numeric perplexity in the abstract. No number recorded.
- **QuaRot (rotation-based outlier removal, W4A4KV4)** (`quantization/quarot`) — w4a4kv4 (weights, activations AND KV cache all at 4 bits); the paper also reports lossless 6-bit and 8-bit round-to-nearest results with no calibration data · CONTESTED between two primary artifacts of the same paper. The arXiv v2 abstract states the 4-bit LLaMa2-70B model has 'losses of at most 0.47 WikiText-2 perplexity and retains 99% of the zero-shot performance'; the repository README states 'at most 0.29 WikiText perplexity' for the same model. Both figures are recorded here rather than picking one; neither was checked against the experiments section, which was not read. The 6-bit and 8-bit lossless claim is stated qualitatively in the abstract only.
- **QuaRot KV cache 4-bit (rotated KV, no retained outlier channels)** (`quantization/quarot-kv4`) — 4-bit KV cache (keys and values), obtained after Hadamard rotation; part of the w4a4kv4 configuration
- **Quest (query-aware KV page sparsity) - NOT KV quantization** (`quantization/quest-kv-sparsity`) — none - no bits reduced. Only the top-K critical KV pages are LOADED for attention; the rest stay in memory but are not read. · From the abstract: up to 2.23x self-attention speedup, reducing inference latency by 7.03x, 'while performing well on tasks with long dependencies with negligible accuracy loss'. The 7.03x is inference latency, not attention latency - the attention number is 2.23x.
- **SGLang hardware-dependent kernel selection logic for FP4/FP8 GEMM** (`quantization/qhw-sglang-kernel-selection`) — varies by backend - W4A16 (Marlin), W4A4 (NVFP4), W8A8 (FP8)
- **ShadowKV (low-rank key cache on GPU, value cache offloaded)** (`quantization/shadowkv`) — none by quantization; keys are compressed by a LOW-RANK representation and values are offloaded to CPU rather than reduced in precision. · From the abstract: supports up to 6x larger batch sizes and boosts throughput by up to 3.04x on an A100 GPU without sacrificing accuracy, evaluated on RULER, LongBench and Needle-In-A-Haystack across Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3-8B-1M, GLM-4-9B-1M, Yi-9B-200K, Phi-3-Mini-128K and Qwen2-7B-128K.
- **SignRound (signed gradient descent for weight rounding optimization)** (`quantization/qhw-signround`) — w4a16 (2-4 bits per weight, with optimized rounding) · From the paper abstract: 'SignRound achieved absolute average accuracy improvements ranging from 6.91% to 33.22% at 2 bits, as measured by the average zero-shot accuracy across 11 tasks.' This is a large improvement over baseline RTN at 2-bit. The paper also claims 'near-lossless 4-bit quantization in most scenarios'. The 6.91-33.22% improvement at 2-bit is the key figure - it shows that optimized rounding matters enormously at very low bit widths. At 4-bit, the improvement is smaller but still positive.
- **Silent precision degradation: when W4A4 formats are served as W4A16 on pre-Blackwell hardware** (`quantization/qhw-silent-precision-degradation`) — w4a4 advertised, w4a16 actual on pre-Blackwell hardware
- **SmoothQuant (W8A8 via offline outlier migration)** (`quantization/smoothquant`) — w8a8 · From the paper, OPT-175B under INT8 with the most aggressive O3 setting: 7 zero-shot benchmarks plus WikiText perplexity, reported as maintaining the FP16 model's accuracy (quant-smoothquant-paper); up to 1.56x speedup and 2x memory reduction, and the v7 body text gives the more precise 1.51x speedup / 1.96x memory saving for OPT-175B, BLOOM-176B, GLM-130B, MT-NLG 530B. No per-benchmark delta table transcribed here - the paper's Table 3 has it and I did not read the cells.
- **SmoothQuant with FP8 activations: does outlier migration still help?** (`quantization/qhw-smoothquant-fp8-interaction`) — w8a8 (8-bit weights, 8-bit activations)
- **SnapKV (observation-window KV selection) - NOT KV quantization** (`quantization/snapkv`) — none - selects important KV POSITIONS per attention head from an observation window; no bits are reduced. · From the abstract: 3.6x increase in generation speed and 8.2x memory-efficiency improvement over baseline at 16K-token inputs, comparable performance across 16 long-sequence datasets, and only a negligible accuracy drop on Needle-in-a-Haystack.
- **SpQR (Sparse-Quantized Representation for near-lossless 3-4 bit compression)** (`quantization/qhw-spqr`) — w4a16 (3-4 bits per weight with sparse outlier preservation) · From the paper abstract: 'relative accuracy losses of less than 1% in perplexity for highly-accurate LLaMA and Falcon LLMs' at 3-4 bits per parameter. This is a stronger claim than GPTQ or AWQ make for the same bit width. The paper also reports '15% speedup' and 'memory compression gains of more than 4x' for a 33B parameter LLM on a single 24 GB consumer GPU. The <1% perplexity loss is the key differentiator: GPTQ at 4-bit typically shows 0.1-0.3 perplexity increase on Llama2-7B (see gptq record), which is already quite good, but SpQR claims to be near-lossless even at 3-bit.
- **SpinQuant (learned rotations + W4A4KV4)** (`quantization/spinquant`) — w4a4 (weights AND activations at 4-bit; also quantizes the KV cache to 4-bit) · From the paper (quant-spinquant-paper): W4A4KV4 on LLaMA-2 7B gives an average zero-shot reasoning accuracy of 64.0, a 2.9-point gap from full precision; LLM-QAT is 22.0 points behind under identical precision, SmoothQuant 25.0 points behind. W4A8 on Mistral-7B reduces the gap to full precision from 12.1 to 1.6 points on zero-shot commonsense reasoning. The paper also reports that merely switching between *random* rotation seeds changes zero-shot accuracy by up to 13 points, which is the finding that motivates learning the rotations.
- **SqueezeLLM (dense-and-sparse quantization, up to 3-bit)** (`quantization/squeezellm`) — 3-bit weights (paper claims lossless compression to ultra-low precisions of up to 3-bit); activations fp16 · From the abstract: on LLaMA models, 3-bit quantization 'significantly reduces the perplexity gap from the FP16 baseline by up to 2.1x as compared to the state-of-the-art methods with the same memory' budget. The 2.1x is a RATIO OF THE GAP, not an absolute perplexity; do not read it as 'PPL is 2.1x worse'.
- **Ternary / 1.58-bit quantization (general)** (`quantization/ternary`) — 1.58 avg (weights in {-1, 0, +1})
- **Transformers bitsandbytes integration (load_in_4bit / load_in_8bit via BitsAndBytesConfig)** (`quantization/bitsandbytes-load-in-4bit`) — 4-bit weights stored as NF4 or FP4; nested/double quantization adds a second pass over the already-quantized weights to store their own scales, saving a further 0.4 bits/parameter. 8-bit path is LLM.int8() · n/a - the transformers doc gives no controlled perplexity delta for the 4-bit path. Null + note.
- **W4A4 (4-bit weights and 4-bit activations, general term)** (`quantization/wq4a4`) — w4a4
- **ZeroQuant v1 (fine-grained hardware-friendly PTQ + layer-by-layer distillation)** (`quantization/zeroquant-v1`) — w8a8 headline; also int4 weights in fully-connected modules with int8 weights in attention and int8 activations (a mixed w4a8 configuration) · From the paper's abstract: INT8 weight+activation is cost-free for BERT and GPT-3 style models with minimal accuracy impact, giving up to 5.19x (BERT) and 4.16x (GPT-3 style) speedup over FP16; on GPT-J 6B and GPT-NeoX 20B the INT8 model achieves accuracy similar to FP16 with up to 5.2x better efficiency. These are speed figures, not a perplexity delta; no PPL number is given in the abstract.
- **ZeroQuant-V2 (systematic PTQ study + low-rank compensation LoRC)** (`quantization/zeroquant-v2`) — study spans w4a16 and w4a8; also covers weight-only and activation-only variants across 125M-176B models · No single number in the abstract. The finding itself is the result: activation quantization is more susceptible to damage than weight quantization, and smaller models often tolerate activation quantization better than larger ones.
- **ZipCache (channel-separable tokenwise KV quantization + salient token identification)** (`quantization/zipcache`) — mixed precision across salient and non-salient tokens; headline is a 4.98x KV compression ratio, not a single bit width · From the abstract: on Mistral-7B / GSM8k, compresses the KV cache by 4.98x with only a 0.38% drop in accuracy. On LLaMA3-8B at input length 4096: 37.3% reduction in prefill-phase latency, 56.9% reduction in decoding-phase latency, 19.8% reduction in GPU memory usage.
- **bitsandbytes NF4 (4-bit NormalFloat)** (`quantization/bitsandbytes-nf4`) — w4a16
- **llmcompressor (Red Hat AI / vLLM project) + compressed-tensors checkpoint format** (`quantization/llmcompressor-quant`) — the scheme set is named, not numeric: FP8_BLOCK, FP8_DYNAMIC, INT8, W2A16..W8A16 (and G32/G64 group variants), MXFP4, MXFP8, NVFP4, plus arbitrary-bit and mixed-precision. The documented worked example is FP8 weights with RTN at block_size 128 and dynamic FP8 activations · n/a - the README ships no controlled fp16 delta. The documented example uses Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B and only says 'Confirm generations of the quantized model look sane'. Null + note.
- **optimum-quanto (Hugging Face quantization library)** (`quantization/optimum-quanto`) — int2 / int4 / int8 / float8 weights (and optional int8/float8 activations) · Qualitative only, from the project README: models compiled with int8/float8 weights and float8 activations are 'very close to the full-precision models', and inference latency with quantized-weights-only is comparable to full precision where optimized kernels exist (quant-quanto-readme). No numeric benchmark delta published - hence quality_delta left as this qualitative statement rather than null only.
- **vLLM quantization backend selection and hardware compatibility** (`quantization/qhw-vllm-kernel-selection`) — varies by method - W4A16 (GPTQ/AWQ/Marlin), W8A8 (FP8/INT8), W4A4 (NVFP4 on Blackwell)

## Interconnect (53)

- **Compute Express Link 2.0** (`interconnect/cxl-2-0`) — 63.0 GB/s · Point-to-point device attachment over PCIe PHY, extended with switching and memory pooling so a single host can reach pooled memory devices across a CXL domain.
- **Compute Express Link 3.x** (`interconnect/cxl-3-x`) — 236.0 GB/s · Switched fabric with memory pooling and multi-host sharing across a CXL domain; peer-to-peer device-to-device traffic is possible within the domain, which is new relative to 2.0.
- **Compute Express Link 4.0** (`interconnect/cxl-4-0`) — 472.0 GB/s · Switched fabric with pooling, now with native x2 width for platform fan-out, bundled ports combining host and Type 1/2 accelerator ports, and support for up to four retimers for channel reach.
- **AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) scale-out network** (`interconnect/aws-efa`) — None GB/s · Standard switched Ethernet data-centre network, with EFA adding the scale-out interface that carries collectives between instances and hosts. EFA is an adapter and its programming model (SRD, an OS-bypass path) is the distinguishing feature rather than any new physical layer - it presents RDMA-style verbs over commodity Ethernet.
- **NVIDIA BlueField-3 DPU** (`interconnect/nic-bluefield3-dpu`) — 50 GB/s · Standard Ethernet or InfiniBand switched fabric. BlueField-3 can operate in either Ethernet or InfiniBand mode.
- **NVIDIA BlueField-4 DPU** (`interconnect/nic-bluefield4-dpu`) — 100 GB/s · Standard Ethernet or InfiniBand switched fabric.
- **NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet Platform** (`interconnect/nic-spectrumx-ethernet`) — 100 GB/s · Leaf-spine Ethernet. Spectrum-X Multiplane scales to 128K GPUs in two tiers.
- **Tenstorrent QSFP-DD fabric (Wormhole 200G, Blackhole 800G)** (`interconnect/tenstorrent-qsfp-dd`) — 25 GB/s · Standard switched Ethernet ports on each card, daisy-chained into racks rather than switched into one large non-blocking domain. Wormhole: 2x QSFP-DD 200G plus 2x Warp 100 Bridge connectors per card. Blackhole: 4x QSFP-DD 800G passive per card, and the in-card Warp bridges are gone from the published Blackhole connectivity row - the architecture change from Wormhole to Blackhole moved scale-up capacity from 200G QSFP-DD plus bridges onto four passive 800G ports. This is a scale-OUT mechanism in the ordinary Ethernet sense, despite Tenstorrent marketing the cards' multi-card capability as scale-up.
- **Ultra Ethernet (UEC) and Ethernet scale-out baseline** (`interconnect/ethernet-uec`) — None GB/s · Switched Ethernet, classically leaf-spine. UEC's design goal is precisely to keep this topology while fixing the collective-communication behaviour that makes commodity Ethernet awkward for AI.
- **InfiniBand XDR (Quantum-2)** (`interconnect/infiniband-xdr`) — 25 GB/s · Switched fat-tree with a centrally managed subnet manager providing routing and multiple paths between nodes, so simple leaf/aggregation/spine switches suffice without per-switch management.
- **NVIDIA ConnectX-7 NDR 400Gb/s InfiniBand HCA** (`interconnect/nic-connectx7-ndr-400gbps`) — 50 GB/s · Switched fat-tree or Dragonfly+ via Quantum-2 switches. ConnectX-7 is the adapter (HCA) endpoint.
- **NVIDIA ConnectX-8 XDR 800Gb/s InfiniBand SuperNIC** (`interconnect/nic-connectx8-xdr-800gbps`) — 100 GB/s · Switched fat-tree or Dragonfly+ via Quantum-X800 switches. ConnectX-8 is the SuperNIC endpoint.
- **NVIDIA Quantum-2 InfiniBand Switch** (`interconnect/nic-quantum2-switch`) — 50 GB/s · Fat-tree, Dragonfly+, multi-dimensional torus. 1U fixed-configuration switch.
- **NVIDIA Quantum-X800 InfiniBand Switch** (`interconnect/nic-quantumx800-switch`) — 100 GB/s · Fat-tree, Dragonfly+. 1U fixed-configuration switch.
- **AMD Infinity Fabric link (4th generation)** (`interconnect/amd-infinity-fabric-link`) — 64 GB/s · Die-to-die links inside a 3D-via Chiplet package, plus package-to-package links wiring up to 8 OAM modules into one platform. The MI325X platform integrates 8 fully connected MI325X OAM modules on an industry-standard OCP design via 4th-generation Infinity Fabric links, giving a fully-connected 8-way scale-up domain.
- **AMD Infinity Fabric link (CDNA 4 / MI350 class)** (`interconnect/amd-infinity-fabric-cdna4`) — 76.8 GB/s · Fully connected 8-GPU node, identical to the prior generation. AMD's MI350 microarchitecture reference (net2-rocm-mi350-microarch) states 'a fully connected 8-GPU node topology, identical to the prior generation' with each GPU reaching its 7 peers over 7 Infinity Fabric links at 38.4 Gbps, plus one PCIe Gen 5 x16 link to the host and 'one Infinity Fabric link configured for PCIe Gen 5 to connect to I/O devices such as storage and networking'. MI350X is an air-cooled 1000W OAM on a UBB8 baseboard that is drop-in compatible with the MI325X platform; MI355X is 1400W direct liquid-cooled, and AMD states up to 128 MI355X fit in a 200kW rack. THE PACKAGE-INTERIOR CHANGE IS THE REAL STORY: CDNA 4 consolidates the I/O dies from four in CDNA 3 to two larger ones, and 'the direct connection between the two IODs reduces latency and power consumption compared to the previous generation' - each IOD now carries four links.
- **NVIDIA NVLink 2.0** (`interconnect/nvlink-2`) — 25 GB/s · Direct point-to-point links between GPU pairs, partial mesh. NVIDIA's Volta datasheet states 'Up to eight V100 accelerators can be interconnected', so 8 GPUs is the practical all-to-all ceiling and it is reached by direct links alone - there is no switch generation below NVSwitch 2. Beyond 8, scale-out requires external networking (InfiniBand or Ethernet, see infiniband-xdr and ethernet-uec).
- **NVIDIA NVLink 3.0** (`interconnect/nvlink-3`) — 25 GB/s · Direct point-to-point links between GPU pairs. All-to-all full mesh is only practical up to 8 GPUs; beyond that, NVSwitch is required to avoid partial connectivity.
- **NVIDIA NVLink 4.0** (`interconnect/nvlink-4`) — 25 GB/s · Point-to-point GPU-to-GPU links, exposed on both sides of the card (NVLink bridge on PCIe SKUs such as H100 NVL, direct in SXM/ HGX baseboards). Switched via NVSwitch 4 for a non-blocking 8-GPU server domain.
- **NVIDIA NVLink 5.0** (`interconnect/nvlink-5`) — 50 GB/s · Direct GPU-to-GPU links on the device, plus switch trays that extend NVLink into a 72-GPU NVLink domain (GB200/GB300 NVL72).
- **NVIDIA NVLink 6.0** (`interconnect/nvlink-6`) — 41.7 GB/s · Direct GPU-to-GPU links plus switch fabric; Vera Rubin NVL72 connects 72 GPUs all-to-all as one non-blocking compute fabric.
- **NVLink 1 (Pascal, Tesla P100)** (`interconnect/nvlink-1`) — 20.0 GB/s · Direct point-to-point links between GPU pairs. With 4 links per GPU an all-to-all mesh is impractical beyond a few GPUs: NVIDIA's own P100 material shows the 8-GPU node as 'up to eight Tesla P100 GPUs interconnected in a single node', reached by grouping the limited links per peer pair rather than by a crossbar.
- **NVIDIA NVLink Switch 2** (`interconnect/nvswitch-2`) — 300 GB/s · Switched, non-blocking within the domain. NVIDIA's HGX A100 table shows NVSwitch absent at 4 GPUs ('N/A') and present at 8 and 16, with the per-GPU rate unchanged at 600 GB/s aggregate across all three sizes - i.e. the switch changes the domain size and removes the mesh topology constraint without changing the per-GPU rate, exactly as it does at later generations.
- **NVIDIA NVLink Switch 4** (`interconnect/nvswitch-4`) — 450 GB/s · Switched, non-blocking all-to-all across an 8-GPU domain inside one server. Every GPU reaches every other GPU at full NVLink rate simultaneously.
- **NVIDIA NVLink Switch 5** (`interconnect/nvswitch-5`) — 900 GB/s · Switched non-blocking fabric supporting both 8-GPU and 72-GPU NVLink domains (GB200/GB300 NVL72).
- **NVSwitch 1 (Volta, DGX-2 / HGX-2)** (`interconnect/nvswitch-1`) — 300.0 GB/s · Switched, non-blocking all-to-all crossbar. The NVLink crossbar reaches 1.98 TB/s of bisection bandwidth at 80% NVLink efficiency (net2-nvidia-nvswitch1-dgx2-blog), so the switch is not the bandwidth limit - the links are. Domain size is the switch's contribution: DGX-2 holds 16 V100 32 GB in one system, versus the partial-mesh 8-GPU nodes that direct attach allowed.
- **NVSwitch 3 (Hopper, H100/H200 - contested generation number)** (`interconnect/nvswitch-3`) — 450.0 GB/s · Switched, non-blocking all-to-all across the 8-GPU domain inside one server, as at NVSwitch 2 and 4. The Hopper generation's real additions are in-network compute and management rather than topology: SHARP in-network reduction and multicast, control-plane resilience, and the ability to run a partially populated rack.
- **AWS NeuronLink (Neuron chip-to-chip scale-up)** (`interconnect/aws-neuronlink`) — 192 GB/s · Non-blocking, and AWS uses that word explicitly. Scale-up domain is one EC2 instance: Inf2 holds up to 12 Inferentia2 chips, Trn2.48xlarge holds 16 Trainium2 chips, and a Trainium2 UltraServer spans 64 chips across 4 instances. The link is chip-to-chip and bypasses the host CPU for transfers, which is the property that makes multi-chip tensor parallelism viable at all - a path through host memory would halve effective bandwidth and add a hop.
- **Biren BLink die-to-die and external I/O (BR100)** (`interconnect/biren-blink`) — None GB/s · Two distinct paths, as with several other records in this repo and easy to conflate. DIE-TO-DIE: the BR100 is a 2-die 7nm chiplet design on CoWoS packaging, the two dies joined by 896 GB/s of 'high speed die-to-die interconnect' (net2-biren-hotchips-br100) - note this is a different mechanism from BR100's four-die successor architecture, and the vendor presents the chiplet split as buying '30% more performance, 20% better yield compared with a monolithic design'. CHIP-TO-CHIP / EXTERNAL I/O: 8 'BLink' connections aggregating to 2.3 TB/s of external I/O bandwidth, with host attach over 'PCIe Gen5 x16 w/CXL' - the w/CXL suffix is worth noting as the only CXL mention in this record's source. SCALE-UP DOMAIN: the server topology slide shows BR100 OAM parts with '8 cards all-to-all interconnection topology', a direct-attached full mesh with no switch part.
- **Cambricon MLU-Link (chiplet / multi-chip scale-up)** (`interconnect/cambricon-mlu-link`) — 200 GB/s · Chiplet-to-chiplet and chip-to-chip, used on the dual-die X4 and X8 variants. The S4 and S8 inference cards are single configurations that do not use MLU-Link for scale-up, so the two are different products in this family rather than different SKUs of one part.
- **Cerebras on-wafer fabric and wafer-to-wafer mesh** (`interconnect/cerebras-wafer-mesh`) — None GB/s · On-wafer fabric: a 2D mesh embedded in the wafer connecting the AI cores, plus HBM attached at the wafer edge - there is no off-package memory tier at all, which is the defining structural difference from every other part in this repo. SCALE-OUT IS BY ADDING WAFERS, and this is the mechanism worth understanding: CS-3 is a single WSE-3 wafer, CS-4 is three WSE-3 Turbo wafers in one system, and Cerebras' stated lever for keeping decode interactive at that size is LATENCY, not bandwidth - CS-4 reduces wafer-to-wafer interconnect latency to 2 microseconds, which the vendor credits with delivering over 1,000 tokens per second on models exceeding 50 trillion parameters. Two microseconds between wafers is the load-bearing figure for this record: a model far larger than any single wafer's SRAM is split across wafers, and every cross-wafer access pays that latency, so the sharding scheme has to be latency-aware in a way it would not be inside one package.
- **Google Cloud TPU Inter-Chip Interconnect (ICI)** (`interconnect/google-tpu-ici`) — 200 GB/s · Switched mesh, NOT a full mesh, and this is the defining difference from the GPU scale-up fabrics. Per generation: v4 uses a 3D mesh that can be reconfigured into a 3D torus, with 6 interconnect links per chip, a 4096-chip pod, and optical circuit switches between cubes - the v4 architecture paper is the source for the optical switching. v5p uses a 3D torus. v5e and v6e both use a 2D TORUS across a 256-chip pod. Google's pod-level docs give the consequences directly as published numbers, which is why those are worth reading instead of deriving a mesh diameter: v5e all-reduce 51.2 TB/s per pod against a BISECTION bandwidth of only 1.6 TB/s; v6e all-reduce 102.4 TB/s against bisection 3.2 TB/s. That ratio is the whole story of ICI versus NVSwitch - a torus gives strong nearest-neighbour and all-reduce performance at a bisection bandwidth roughly 30x lower than the all-reduce figure, whereas nvswitch-4's 8-GPU domain is non-blocking.
- **Groq LPU chip-to-chip network** (`interconnect/groq-lpu-interconnect`) — None GB/s · Not published. What IS published is the determinism property: because Groq statically schedules all data movement at compile time, the multi-chip topology is fixed at tapeout rather than dynamically routed, so there are no dynamic scheduling stalls and no cache misses across chips. That architectural property is the load-bearing claim here and it is qualitative - the vendor asserts it, but no link rate, latency or topology diagram is given.
- **HBM3 on-package memory bus** (`interconnect/hbm3-memory-bus`) — 5325 GB/s · On-package, on the same interposer as the compute dies. Not a fabric - there are no cables, no switches, no topology, and no distance.
- **Huawei HCCS (Hierarchical Chip-to-Chip Scale)** (`interconnect/huawei-hccs`) — 30 GB/s · Point-to-point chip-to-chip ports, three per accelerator, giving roughly 90 GB/s of chip-to-chip bandwidth per part. No switch part is documented in the sources retrieved; the 910B systems scale out with many chips and Huawei's software stack (CANN) is what manages the collective traffic.
- **Huawei UB Link 2.0 (Ascend 950DT scale-up / unified addressing)** (`interconnect/huawei-ub-link`) — 392.0 GB/s · Two scale-up domains at different rates, which is unusual and is the interesting property of this record. INTRA-SERVER: 8 NPUs on the Atlas 650E (14U air-cooled, ~14.5 kW, 2 x 950 CPUs), 8 x 96 GB on-chip memory = 768 GB, 4.0 TB/s peak memory bandwidth per server. FULL-MESH: 16 NPUs at the doubled 1.68 TB/s bidirectional per NPU, i.e. Huawei publishes a wider non-mesh-free domain than the 8-way that AMD's Infinity Fabric and NVIDIA's NVSwitch both top out at. SUPER-POD: the 44OU Atlas 950 SuperPoD cabinet holds 64 NPUs at ~100 kW liquid-cooled and scales to 1024 NPUs, '1.72 PB/s UB Link' across the pod, which is 1.72 PB/s / 1024 = 1.72 TB/s per NPU bidirectional, or 860 GB/s per direction - essentially flat with the 16-NPU full-mesh rate, meaning Huawei scales bandwidth with NPU count rather than holding a flat per-chip figure.
- **Huawei Unified Bus (UB) — Ascend 910C / CloudMatrix 384 scale-up fabric** (`interconnect/huawei-ub`) — 196.0 GB/s · Two-level switching: L1 on-board switching (7 UB Switch chips per compute node, each NPU connected to all 7 switches at 28 GB/s per port) and L2 rack-level switching (112 L2 UB switch chips across 4 communication racks, 7 sub-planes x 16 chips each, each sub-plane an independent 384-port full-mesh network). The system uses 6,912 800G LPO optical transceivers for entirely optical intra- and inter-rack connectivity. Scale-out is separate: 200 Gbps RoCE RDMA per NPU (76.8 Tbps total).
- **MetaX MetaXLink (multi-GPU interconnect)** (`interconnect/metaxlink`) — 896.0 GB/s · 8-card full-interconnect topology. MetaX's C550 product page states 'MetaXLink interconnect enables an 8-card full-interconnect topology.' The C550 3D Mesh Supernode supports up to 8 servers and 64 cards with 3D Mesh topology. No switch part is named.
- **Moore Threads MTLink (MTT S4000 card-to-card fabric)** (`interconnect/moore-threads-mtlink`) — 120.0 GB/s · Physical card-to-card links via an MTLink Bridge accessory. The S4000 page states the MTLink Bridge supports 2-, 4- and 8-card topologies, which is a small direct-attached domain comparable to the 8-way meshes AMD's Infinity Fabric provides and smaller than what NVSwitch reaches. No switch part is named in the retrieved sources.
- **Tenstorrent Warp 100 Bridge (Wormhole in-card / adjacent-card link)** (`interconnect/tenstorrent-warp100`) — None GB/s · Adjacent-card bridge, physical. The Warp 100 Bridge is a plug-in card that links two Wormhole cards installed next to each other in the same host, keyed to a specific orientation and typically pre-installed in Tenstorrent Galaxy systems. Each card supports up to two bridges. n300d and n300s cards use 2.5-slot coolers and can therefore only take the triple-slot bridge. This is a mechanically simple, low-port-count, same-chassis link - there is no switch part and no topology beyond 'the two cards this bridge spans'.
- **UALink 200G 1.0** (`interconnect/ualink-200g-1-0`) — 25 GB/s · Multi-layer fabric (UPLI protocol / transaction / data link / physical). Consortium-supported topologies: mesh and ring for small clusters of 4-16 nodes, torus for mid-scale, SWITCHED POD as the primary deployment model scaling to hundreds or thousands of accelerators, and direct-attach for small clusters. Complex ring and torus topologies are explicitly out of specification scope and need care to avoid deadlocks.
- **UCIe-Advanced on-chip mesh (Rebellions Rebel100 chiplets)** (`interconnect/rebellions-ucie`) — 125 GB/s · FULL-CHIP MESH, and this is the distinguishing property. All four homogeneous chiplets of one Rebel100 are connected by a full-mesh on-chip fabric over UCIe-Advanced, so the four present to software as a single virtual die with no software-visible boundary and no I/O bottleneck - the vendor's explicit claim. At 11 ns latency that is roughly a register-to-register hop. The mesh is backed by hardware-accelerated full-mesh synchronization across 256 cores. Contrast with amd-xgmi, which is also a die-to-die mesh but only 2 or 8 dies, and with every GPU part in this repo, where crossing between devices is a real and measurable cost.
- **PCI Express 3.0** (`interconnect/pcie-gen3`) — 15.75 GB/s · Point-to-point host-to-device (root complex to endpoint), up to 16 lanes. Becomes a shared fabric only via PCIe switches or host bridges.
- **PCI Express 4.0** (`interconnect/pcie-gen4`) — 31.5 GB/s · Point-to-point host-to-device (root complex to endpoint), up to 16 lanes. Becomes a shared fabric only via PCIe switches or host bridges.
- **PCI Express 5.0** (`interconnect/pcie-gen5`) — 63.0 GB/s · Point-to-point host-to-device by default (root complex to endpoint), up to 16 lanes. Becomes a shared fabric only through PCIe switches or host bridges, in which case ordering and oversubscription apply.
- **PCI Express 6.0** (`interconnect/pcie-gen6`) — 236.0 GB/s · Point-to-point host-to-device, up to 16 lanes, with flit-level framing and signalling changes versus PCIe 5.0. Shares the physical layer with CXL 4.0.
- **PCIe Gen5 x16 host link (128 GB/s, unchanged across CDNA3/CDNA4)** (`interconnect/amd-pcie-gen5-x16`) — 128 GB/s · Host-to-GPU (tree topology via root complex). Each GPU has one PCIe Gen5 x16 link to the host. In a dual-socket 8-GPU system, 4 GPUs are connected to each socket's root complex.
- **RoCE (RDMA over Converged Ethernet)** (`interconnect/roce`) — None GB/s · Any Ethernet topology that can carry lossless RDMA - typically a leaf-spine fabric, but constrained by the requirement for lossless operation (PFC / priority flow control, DCB) and typically single-path rather than multi-path. Contrast with InfiniBand, which gets losslessness and multipath from the subnet manager.
- **NVIDIA NVLink-C2C (second generation)** (`interconnect/nvlink-c2c`) — 900 GB/s · Point-to-point die-to-die chip-to-chip link. Integrates at PCB level, in a multi-chip module, or across a silicon interposer / wafer-level connection. One such link joins a Grace CPU to a Hopper GPU (GH200), two Grace CPUs to each other, or two Blackwell GPUs plus a Grace CPU in GB200.
- **UFI (Ultra Express Fabric)** (`interconnect/ufi-ultra-express-fabric`) — None GB/s
- **AMD Infinity Fabric scale-up link (CDNA3: 128 GB/s per direction)** (`interconnect/amd-infinity-fabric-link-cdna3`) — 128 GB/s · Fully connected 8-GPU mesh (each GPU connects to 7 others). No switch. 7 links per GPU for GPU-to-GPU communication. 8th link in the board spec is for scale-out (external). Scale-up bandwidth: 128 GB/s per direction per link.
- **AMD Infinity Fabric scale-up link (CDNA4: 153.6 GB/s per direction, 20% faster)** (`interconnect/amd-infinity-fabric-link-cdna4`) — 153.6 GB/s · Fully connected 8-GPU mesh (each GPU connects to 7 others). No switch. 7 links per GPU for GPU-to-GPU communication. Identical topology to CDNA3. The MI355X product page lists 'Infinity Fabric Links: 7' and 'Peak Infinity Fabric Link Bandwidth: 153 GB/s' (rounded). Scale-out link: 128 GB/s (unchanged from CDNA3).
- **AMD xGMI (Socket/Inter-Chip Global Memory Interconnect)** (`interconnect/amd-xgmi`) — 50 GB/s · Point-to-point, no switch part. TWO distinct roles, and this is the part that is routinely misread: (1) DIE-TO-DIE, inside one package - on MI250X the two GCDs of one OAM module are joined by FOUR xGMI/Infinity Fabric links, which AMD gives as 4 x 25 GT/sec = 200 GB/sec peak transfer between the two GCDs, or 400 GB/sec bidirectional for the same; (2) DIE-TO-DEVICE, between accelerators - on MI210 (PCIe cards) xGMI is exposed through direct-connect xGMI BRIDGE CARDS in adjacent PCIe slots, giving dual and quad GPU hives, whereas the MI250X/MI250 OAM modules carry 8 links natively. On a multi-OAM MI300X node AMD's own architecture reference states the accelerator-side count is SEVEN Infinity Fabric links, used 'to form a fully connected 8-GPU system' - but the MI300X product page board table says 'Infinity Fabric Links: 8'. That is a real disagreement between two first-party AMD sources, not a typo: seven links is the minimum needed to make 8 nodes fully connected (each node needs a link to each of the other 7), so the board-table 8 is most likely counting an extra link of a different role (host or scale-out) rather than a mesh edge. Both figures are retained here; the typed link_count field carries the die-to-die value of 4 for MI250X, which is where this record's per-link rate is sourced. On CDNA3/MI300 the die-to-die topology is also a full mesh over up to 8 vertically stacked XCDs plus 4 I/O dies, so an MI300X is internally a single 8-way domain, not two halves.
